# Expected skips on the unprivileged Linux lanes: ubuntu-latest (amd64),
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (arm64), and the GOEXPERIMENT=runtimesecret variant of
# both. Derived from the t.Skip sites in the source and what the hosted
# runners provide, not measured on a runner: the first red run corrects it.
#
# Deliberately NOT listed, because ubuntu-latest kernels have memfd_secret
# live and the parent may ptrace its child under Yama's default scope:
# TestMemfdIsolation_HoldsAfterMapFixed, TestExternalExtraction_*,
# TestMadvise_MemfdSecretTierFlagsInForce, TestMadviseBeforeFree_*. If one of
# those skips, the isolation proof has stopped running and the job must say so.

# GitHub's hosted pool mixes CPU generations and does not guarantee AVX-512,
# so Z16–Z31 may not exist; the proof runs wherever they do. amd64 only —
# the file is not compiled on arm64, so the entry is unused there.
github.com/deadpoets/secmem TestScrub_ClearsVectorRegistersZMMHi

# The success path is verified out-of-process in TestHelpersIsolated; this
# test is the ErrUnsupported pin for platforms without a core-dump rlimit.
github.com/deadpoets/secmem TestDisableCoreDumps_Unsupported

# The forced-exit status only has to match the OS default on Windows.
github.com/deadpoets/secmem TestForcedExitStatus_MatchesUninterceptedSignal

# PR_SET_MEMORY_MERGE needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE; the child skips with EPERM
# here. The root lane (linux-root.txt) runs this proof and may not skip it.
github.com/deadpoets/secmem TestMadvise_UnmergeableInForce

# Seed #1 is the empty plaintext: a zero-length buffer is refused by the core
# by design, so this seed skips on every platform.
github.com/deadpoets/secmem/secmem-crypto FuzzOpenInto_RoundTrip/seed#1
